{{Quote|The piscine Jedi with the upside-down features looked fearsome!|An artist, in his journal|<ref name="Star Wars: Alien Archive">''[[Star Wars: Alien Archive]]''</ref>}}
'''Pablo-Jill''' was an [[Ongree]]<ref name="Episode II" /> [[Gender|male]] [[Jedi Knight]]<ref name="Force Collection" /> that participated in the [[First Battle of Geonosis]] as a part of the [[Jedi assault team]]. Pablo-Jill fought alongside the Jedi to free [[Jedi Knight]]s [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], and [[Anakin Skywalker]], along with [[Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]] from the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]].<ref name="Episode II" /> [[Time|Sometime]] during the [[Clone Wars]], [[Pablo-Jill's lightsaber]] was stolen from floating debris by Separatist [[General]] [[Grievous]] following an intense [[Duel over Duro|duel]] over [[Duro]] in a [[Unidentified satellite city|satellite city]] that left Pablo-Jill injured.<ref name="Lightsabers">''[[Star Wars Lightsabers: A Guide to Weapons of the Force]]''</ref> Though encouraged by the [[Jedi Order]] to take a [[Padawan]], Pablo-Jill never chose one.<ref name="Force Collection" /> Pablo-Jill wore [[Jedi apparel|Jedi robes]] and owned a [[Color|blue]]-bladed [[Pablo-Jill's lightsaber|lightsaber]].<ref name="Episode II" />

Between [[19 BBY]] and [[9 BBY]], Pablo-Jill<ref name="Death" /> had been found and executed by the [[Inquisitor]]s. His body was then taken and [[Jedi tomb|entombed]] in their headquarters, the [[Fortress Inquisitorius]], on the [[ocean]] [[moon]] of [[Nur]] in the [[Mustafar system]]. Left in a petrified state, his corpse was left next to those of dozens of other Jedi.<ref name="Part IV">{{Kenobi|Part IV}}</ref> In [[9 BBY]],<ref name="Death" /> Kenobi [[Rescue of Princess Leia (9 BBY)|broke into]] the Fortress Inquisitorius to rescue [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] but discovered Pablo-Jill's corpse and those of the Empire's other Jedi victims. Although disturbed, Kenobi pushed on and completed his mission.<ref name="Part IV" />

==Behind the scenes==
Pablo-Jill is named after a VFX Supervisor and Producer team at [[Industrial Light & Magic]] that worked on the [[2002]] film [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']],<ref name="Pablo-Jill gender">{{Twitter|pablohidalgo|status/821458624119590912|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=@EdinJusovic That is an Ongree named Pablo-Jill. His name (honestly) has nothing to do with me.|nolove=1|nobackup=1}}</ref> [[Pablo Helman]] and [[Jill Brooks]].<ref name="ILM">{{Twitter|pabl0hidalgo|status/1728156451838038252|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=No, he's named after Pablo Helman and Jill Brooks of ILM.|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/MbxYf}}</ref> Pablo-Jill was one of few completely [[Computer/Legends|computer]]-generated characters in the [[Prequel trilogy]]. He was one of only three CGI Jedi in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']]. Because of Pablo-Jill's awkward, bulky form and multi-jointed legs, it was decided that he would look best using computer animation.<ref name="DB">{{DB|character|pablojill|Pablo-Jill}}</ref> There was originally some confusion between Pablo-Jill and the Ongree member of the Jedi Council seen in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']], with early Set Diaries naming the other Ongree Pablo-Jill and later [[Sweitt Concorkill]], though he was eventually named [[Coleman Kcaj]]. The character was originally meant to be Pablo-Jill, but because the Ongree in Episode III needed a more detailed CGI model, a new character was created.<ref name="Hyperspace-Mocking Heads">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/postnotes/news20040227.html|series=Episode III Post Notes|text=Mocking Heads}}</ref><ref name="Hyperspace-Jedi Council Musical Chairs">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/postnotes/news20031125.html|series=Episode III Post Notes|text=Jedi Council Musical Chairs}}</ref><ref name="Hyperspace-Episode III Set Diary - The Jedi Council Puzzle">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/episode-iii/bts/setdiary/news20040828.html|series=Episode III Set Diary|text=The Jedi Council Puzzle}}</ref>

Initially upon the release of [[Part IV]] of ''[[Star Wars: Obi-Wan Kenobi]]'', the Jedi present in Fortress Inquisitorius was identified as Coleman Kcaj on [[StarWars.com]].<ref name="Episode Guide">{{SW|url=series/obi-wan-kenobi/part-iv-guide|text=Part IV Episode Guide | Obi-Wan Kenobi}}</ref> Nevertheless, in the concept art done by [[Kouji Tajima]], the art for this character was instead labeled as Pablo-Jill.<ref name="ArtStation">{{ArtStation|username=koujitajima|url=artwork/NGPvWz|name=[[Kouji Tajima]]|text=Pablo Jill - Obi Wan Kenobi}}</ref> [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] member [[Pablo Hidalgo]] pointed out the Ongree in ''Obi-Wan Kenobi'' does not have spots, closer resembling Pablo-Jill,<ref name="Spots">{{Twitter|pabl0hidalgo|status/1727031570991903218|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=Coleman has spots. Pablo-Jill doesn't. I assumed it was PJ based on that (I think the asset is just called triangle-head).|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/CWmlZ}}</ref> (though in the films neither have spots on their face) but recommended that [[Wookieepedia]] give priority to StarWars.com than the concept art.<ref name="Wookieepedia">{{Twitter|pabl0hidalgo|status/1727049589969260995|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=I'd recommend they follow starwars-com's lead rather than take my assumptions to heart.|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/aa2Uy}}</ref> Starwars.com later changed the mention of Kcaj to Pablo-Jill.<ref name="Episode Guide" />
